map_lists:
- Read and follow PEP 8 style guidelines.
- Use only UNIX style newlines (`\n`).
- Wrap long lines in parentheses instead of using backslashes for line continuation.
- Use specific exception types in `except` clauses (e.g., `except Exception:`) rather than bare `except:`.
- Include your name in TODO comments (e.g., `# TODO(yourname)`).
- Do not use author tags in source files.
- Do not put vim configuration in source files.
- Delay string interpolations at logging calls.
- Do not import eventlet; use threading or asyncio instead.
- Do not shadow built-in or reserved words.
- Use `LOG.warning` instead of the deprecated `Log.warn`.
- Import modules rather than objects, with specific exceptions for stdlib `collections.abc`, `types`, `typing`, third-party `sqlalchemy`, type hinting objects, and `i18n` function imports.
- Do not import more than one module per line.
- Do not use wildcard `*` imports.
- Do not make relative imports.
- Alphabetically order imports by full module path.
- Organize imports into stdlib, third-party, and project groups, separated by blank lines.
- Ensure docstrings do not start with a space.
- End multi-line docstrings on a new line.
- Start multi-line docstrings without a leading new line.
- Start multi-line docstrings with a one-line summary followed by an empty line.
- Split dictionary or list items with newlines if the object exceeds 80 characters.
- Indent items in embedded iterables.
- Add a trailing comma to the last item in dictionaries and lists.
- Do not use `locals()` or `self.__dict__` for formatting strings.
- Format method call arguments with newlines if the call exceeds 80 characters.
- Break up parameter construction into separate variables rather than constructing them inline.
- Internationalize template strings before performing variable replacement.
- Use keyword parameters for multiple variables in internationalized strings.
- Create unit tests for every new feature.
- Add a failing unit test for bug fixes that previously lacked tests.
- Use the most specific exception possible when asserting raised exceptions.
- Do not test for generic `Exception` being raised.
- Use `assertIsNone` or `assertIsNotNone` instead of `assertEqual` with `None`.
- Use `assertEqual` or `assertNotEqual` instead of `assertTrue`/`assertFalse` with equality checks.
- Use `assertGreater`, `assertLess`, `assertGreaterEqual`, or `assertLessEqual` instead of `assertTrue`/`assertFalse` with comparison operators.
- Require `autospec`, `spec`, or `spec_set` in `mock.patch()` or `mock.patch.object()` calls.
- Use `assertIsInstance` instead of `assertTrue(isinstance(A, B))`.
- Use `assertIsInstance` instead of `assertEqual(type(A), B)`.
- Do not use the deprecated `assertRaisesRegexp`.
- Use `assertIn` or `assertNotIn` instead of `assertTrue`/`assertFalse` with `in`/`not in` checks.
- Use `assertIn` or `assertNotIn` instead of `assertEqual` with `in` checks.
- Use `unittest.mock` instead of the third-party `mock` library.
- License newly contributed source code under the Apache 2.0 license.
- Include the Apache 2.0 license header or SPDX identifier in all source files.
- Leave files with no code completely empty, without license headers or comments.
